# Enhancing Safety with AI Monitoring

By Xanrel Torvik, Robotics Research Lead, ConstructAI Lab

Construction sites are among the most hazardous workplaces, with injuries often caused by slips, trips, and unsafe equipment use. Over the past two years, our team at ConstructAI Lab has studied how machine learning (ML) can actively reduce these risks through continuous, real-time monitoring.

Last summer, we deployed a pilot system on a mid-sized urban development called Greenfield Tower. The system combined drone surveys and fixed-site cameras equipped with ML models trained to detect safety violations—such as missing harnesses, unattended tools, or unsafe scaffolding. Within weeks, the system flagged a repeated failure to secure rebar cages properly. Site managers acted immediately, preventing what could have resulted in serious injury or a costly structural failure. This incident underscored the practical value of AI-driven oversight.

Machine learning excels here because it processes vast visual data far faster than human supervisors. Unlike random manual inspections, ML systems provide consistent coverage without fatigue or distraction. They also generate actionable alerts, allowing targeted interventions rather than broad safety reminders.

Based on our findings, we recommend construction firms adopt ML monitoring as a complement—not a replacement—to human safety officers. Start with high-risk zones like rebar tying and scaffolding assembly, where automation can catch subtle yet critical infractions. Invest in tailored ML models trained on site-specific workflows to minimize false alarms. And crucially, integrate these tools into existing safety protocols to enhance accountability and worker trust.

In sum, machine learning is transforming construction safety from reactive to proactive. When thoughtfully deployed, it saves lives and builds stronger, more resilient projects.
